page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.n2.medium is a general-purpose virtual machine instance based on the KVM hypervisor. It features an x86_64 architecture powered by an Intel Xeon 8269CY processor running at 2.5 GHz. The instance is configured with 2 dedicated vCPUs and 2 physical cores, paired with 8.0 GB of system memory, yielding a resource density of 4.0 GB per core. This instance does not include any local storage or GPU accelerators, relying entirely on network-attached storage for its operating system and data volumes.

Performance benchmarks indicate that the ecs.n2.medium operates on the lower end of the performance spectrum. In stress-ng testing, single-core performance scored 1107.09 (bottom 25%) and multi-core performance reached 2193.58 (bottom 10%). Memory bandwidth is also constrained, with large-block read-only bandwidth measured at 16.61 GB/sec and write bandwidth at 14.38 GB/sec. These limitations are reflected in application-level benchmarks, where static web serving throughput is restricted to 1.69 GB/sec and database operations score 553.1 on PassMark, both falling into the bottom 10% of tested instances.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the ecs.n2.medium offers a low-cost entry point for workloads that do not demand high-throughput processing or intensive memory operations. Given its dedicated CPU allocation, it provides more predictable performance than shared-core burstable instances, though its overall processing capacity remains modest. This profile makes it suitable for lightweight utility services, development and testing environments, basic web serving, and low-volume Redis caching, where high-performance hardware is not economically justified.
